title: Tenant Traffic Isolation and SLA Communication Playbook
author: Marisol Vega
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the operational pattern we use to isolate a tenant's traffic during high-risk windows (go-live, model upgrades, major migrations) while preserving global SLAs and providing clear communication to customers and internal stakeholders. It describes configuration primitives (traffic shielding, throttles, priority routing), monitoring assertions, escalation thresholds, and communication templates.

Scope and audience

- Scope: Enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private tenants) undergoing cutovers, model upgrades, or other traffic-impacting activities. Applicable to hosted customers when managed by customer-success/SRE.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Oncall SREs, Platform Engineers, Account Executives, and Support Engineers.

Goals

1. Prevent noisy or migrating tenants from impacting other customers.
2. Maintain observable, measurable SLOs during cutover windows.
3. Provide clear, time-bounded customer communications and escalation playbooks.
4. Standardize tools and APIs for temporary traffic isolation and re-provisioning.

Definitions

- Traffic shielding: temporary routing and rate-limit policies applied to a tenant to constrain or shape its request volume during a cutover.
- Priority routing: assigning higher priority to control-plane or canary requests vs bulk migrate requests.
- SLA guardrail: a monitoring rule that triggers an internal escalation when global or per-tenant SLOs are in danger.

Key SLOs and thresholds (examples)

- Global availability (all tenants): 99.95% daily success rate for control-plane APIs.
- Tenant p99 latency (text-generation endpoint): must not regress > 25% from baseline for >15 minutes.
- Error rate surge (per-tenant): > 0.5% increase in 5m error rate vs rolling baseline => paging threshold.

Prerequisites (before applying traffic shielding)

- Customer cutover runbook approved and time-window scheduled.
- Baseline telemetry captured (last 7 days) for: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, token cost.
- Contact list for customer stakeholders and internal owners (CSM, SE, SRE PM).
- Canary route defined and smoke tests prepared.

Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Primary responsibilities | On-call contact |
|---|---|---|
| CSM | Customer comms, approval, commercial sign-off | name@redwood.ai |
| Platform/SRE | Implement shield, monitor SLOs, operate rollback | oncall-sre@redwood.ai |
| Support Engineer | First-response triage, customer updates | support@redwood.ai |
| Solutions Engineer | Validate integration, run post-cutover validation tests | se-team@redwood.ai |

Pre-cutover checklist (day -2 to -0)

1. Complete telemetry snapshot: run the baseline capture script and attach output to runbook.
2. Verify throttles and shielding profiles are staged in feature-flag system.
3. Run canary traffic to validated canary endpoints and collect artifact logs.
4. Confirm backup config: pre-approved rollback policy and access to reverse throttles.
5. Send T-24h confirmation email to customer with expectations (template included below).

Traffic shielding patterns and examples

We support three common patterns: soft-shield, hard-throttle, and priority-fanout. Use the pattern that matches the risk profile.

1) Soft-shield (recommended for low-risk migrations)
- Limit concurrent requests to a tenant to a percentage of baseline (e.g., 50%).
- Enable burst buffer of +10% for 3 minutes to avoid coupling with retry storms.

2) Hard-throttle (for noisy tenants or emergency mitigation)
- Set absolute RPS or tokens-per-minute ceiling.
- Queue excess requests with 503/Retry-After header for short windows.

3) Priority-fanout (for staged cutovers)
- Route canary and control-plane traffic over a high-priority path.
- Route bulk migration SDK jobs to an isolated worker pool with lower priority.

Sample topology table

| Component | Purpose | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Edge proxy | Apply tenant-level rate limits | Envoy route + rate limit service |
| Ingress gateway | Tenant routing + header enrichment | Nginx + feature flag header |
| Router service | Priority routing, canary gating | internal-router service v2 |
| Worker pool | Isolated fanout for migration jobs | Dedicated pool (dedicated-tenant-pool) |

Operational configuration examples

- Envoy rate-limit descriptor (YAML snippet):

---
actions:
  - request_headers:
      header_name: "x-tenant-id"
  - remote_address: {}

domain: "tenant-shielding"
rate_limit_service:
  transport_api_version: V3
---

- Example API call to set tenant throttle (curl):

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://ops.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/\{tenant_id\}/shield \
  -d '{"mode":"soft-shield","concurrency_pct":50,"burst_seconds":180}'

Prometheus assertions and alert rules (examples)

1) Tenant error rate surge (5m):
- Expression: (increase(redwood_request_errors_total{tenant_id=~"__TENANT__"}[5m]) / increase(redwood_requests_total{tenant_id=~"__TENANT__"}[5m])) > 0.005
- Severity: page if true for 5m.

2) Global p99 latency regression (15m):
- Expression: (quantile_over_time(0.99, redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="frontend"}[15m])) / (quantile_over_time(0.99, redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="frontend"}[7d])) > 1.25
- Severity: page SRE, notify CSM.

3) Shielding effectiveness check (10m):
- Expression: rate(redwood_requests_total{tenant_id=~"__TENANT__",shielded="true"}[10m]) < (baseline_rate{tenant_id=~"__TENANT__"} * 1.1)
- Severity: alert to Platform if shielding not limiting.

Emergency escalation matrix (timeline-based)

- t+0–10m: Support engineer handles initial triage. If blocking, escalate to oncall SRE.
- t+10–30m: Oncall SRE applies temporary hard-throttle if tenant continues to degrade global SLOs. Page Platform lead.
- t+30–60m: If SLA impact persists, CSM notifies customer with priority incident communication and reverts to previously-known-good configuration.
- >60m: Cross-functional incident bridge; potential SLA credits evaluation (follow finance/legal process).

Communication templates

- T-24h confirmation (email subject): "[Redwood] Scheduled migration window for <customer-name> — Confirming plan and expectations"

Body (shortened):
Hi <Customer-Contact>,

This is a reminder that your scheduled migration is planned for <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>. During the window we will apply traffic shielding to manage risk. Expected impact: short delays (sub-1s) for non-control traffic; no data loss expected. If you need to change the window, reply by <T-6h>.

Point-of-contact: <CSM name> (<csm@redwood.ai>), Oncall SRE: oncall-sre@redwood.ai

- Incident start Slack template (private channel to customer + internal):
"Incident: Tenant <tenant-id> shielding applied at <time>. Observed p99 latency = <value> (baseline <value>). Next update in 15 minutes. CSM: <name>. Support runbook: <link>"

Rollback and safe-failback procedures

1. If the shield does not reduce impact after 15 minutes, apply hard-throttle to 20% of baseline and reroute migration traffic to the isolated worker pool.
2. If global SLOs remain violated after 30 minutes, revert all routing to the pre-cutover configuration and drain the migration worker pool.
3. Post-rollback, run a short smoke test and schedule a post-mortem within 72 hours.

Post-cutover validation (t+0–24h)

- Run the standard validation suite: 50 control-plane requests / minute to verify baseline, 10 synthetic journeys for embedding/latency correctness.
- Capture telemetry: 24h delta report (requests, p50/p95/p99, errors, token cost).
- Customer confirmation: send go/no-go closure form and collect CSAT input.

Ticketing and documentation: artifacts to attach

- Baseline telemetry dump (CSV/JSON).
- Shield configuration applied (YAML or API payload).
- All Slack/Email communications (copy).
- Post-mortem notes and action items.

Ownership and contacts

- Platform Oncall: oncall-sre@redwood.ai
- Customer Success: customer-success@redwood.ai
- Support (Escalations): support-escalations@redwood.ai
- Engineering Pager (urgent): +1-555-0100 (Pager duty)

Example telemetry assertion (JSON)

{
  "assertion": "p99_latency_not_regressing",
  "tenant_id": "__TENANT__",
  "window": "15m",
  "threshold": "1.25x_baseline",
  "action": "page-sre-and-notify-csm"
}

Runbook checklist (quick reference)

1. Confirm baseline snapshot present.
2. Apply soft-shield via ops API: run curl command above.
3. Run canary traffic for 10m.
4. Monitor Prometheus rules and Grafana dashboard (tenant cutover panel).
5. If >5m of sustained regression: escalate per matrix.
6. If shielding fails: apply hard-throttle and re-route.
7. Post-cutover: collect artifacts and close ticket.
